name: language-mode-registry
purpose: Defines selectable Korean, English, and all-language document viewing modes for repository dashboards, monitor UIs, generated snapshots, and future desktop surfaces.

reader_guide.summary: Use this registry when a UI or document browser needs to show only Korean documents, only English documents, or every collected document. This is a display lens, not translation or authorization.
how_to_read: Read mode_boundary first so language_mode is not confused with view_mode, work_mode, install_mode, or source-code language filters.
Use supported_languages to understand the file suffixes and BCP 47 language tags recognized by repository collectors.
Use modes[].included_languages and modes[].include_unknown to decide which documents remain visible.
Keep default_mode stable unless the owner changes the repository-wide viewing default.
Treat unknown documents as mixed or language-neutral records; single-language modes hide them by default to honor 'only Korean' and 'only English' views.
update_triggers: A new document language becomes a first-class workspace language.
Workspace Monitor or a desktop UI changes document language filtering behavior.
File suffix conventions for paired Korean and English docs change.
The default repository document language view changes.
Static export, routing, or deployment constraints make route-level internationalization desirable or impossible.

structure_rules.rule: language_mode controls which collected documents are visible in a UI; it does not translate content and does not remove data from generated snapshots by itself.
structure_rules.reason: The user asked for Korean-only and English-only viewing modes, not a translation pipeline or security boundary.

structure_rules.rule: language_mode must stay independent from view_mode, work_mode, install_mode, and source-code language filters.
structure_rules.reason: Audience role, task strictness, setup profile, programming language, and document language answer different questions.

structure_rules.rule: First-class document language ids should use stable BCP 47 primary language tags such as ko and en unless a more specific tag becomes necessary.
structure_rules.reason: Simple, standard language ids are easier to share across collectors, UI filters, and future desktop surfaces.

structure_rules.rule: Korean-only and English-only modes hide unknown-language documents unless a future mode explicitly opts in with include_unknown=true.
structure_rules.reason: A single-language view should mean only that language is visible; mixed or unsuffixed records can be reviewed in all-language mode.

field_guide.meaning: Explains what language_mode controls and how it differs from other workspace modes.

mode_boundary.language_mode: Document-language viewing lens for repository docs, history, requirements, specs, and generated previews.
mode_boundary.view_mode: Audience and UI surface lens such as user, developer, or superadmin developer.
mode_boundary.work_mode: Task execution and close-out strictness profile.
mode_boundary.source_language_filter: Programming-language filter for read-only source code browsing.
mode_boundary.rule: Choose language_mode for Korean/English document visibility. Choose view_mode for role surfaces, work_mode for process strictness, install_mode for setup, and source_language_filter for code files.

modes.label: All Languages
modes.intent: Show Korean, English, and language-neutral documents together for full repository review.
modes.document_rule: Show documents tagged ko, en, or unknown.

modes.label: Korean Only
modes.intent: Show only Korean documents for owner-facing reading, history review, and Korean documentation work.

modes.label: English Only
modes.intent: Show only English documents for paired English review, external sharing, and prompt/config companion checks.

selection_rules: Use all-language mode for governance audits, snapshot publication review, and checking unsuffixed operational records.
Use Korean-only mode when the owner wants to read history, summaries, requirements, and docs without English companion noise.
Use English-only mode when reviewing English companion docs, external-facing summaries, or executable prompt companion material.
Do not use language_mode to hide sensitive documents from a public snapshot; remove or redact those records at collection or publication time.
